generated_content.title: Fox Develops Two-Hour Remake of 1975 Cult Classic 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show'
generated_content.overview: Fox is developing a two-hour remake of the 1975 cult classic musical 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show,' directed, executive-produced, and choreographed by Kenneth Ortega. The special, tentatively titled 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show Event,' is casting-contingent and will be filmed in advance. The project is timed to celebrate the 40th anniversary of the film, which has grossed over $112 million.
key_points: The remake is the latest musical to get the small-screen treatment.
Kenneth Ortega, known for his work on 'High School Musical,' is attached to direct, executive-produce, and choreograph the special.
The special will be produced by Fox 21 Television Studios and The Jackal Group, with Gail Berman and Lou Adler also serving as executive producers.
This isn't the first attempt at adapting 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show,' as Fox previously unveiled plans for an adaptation in 2002 that never came to fruition.
important_facts: $112 million grossed by the original film, which still plays in theaters across the country.
Kenneth Ortega's credits include 'Gilmore Girls,' 'This Is It,' and 'Hocus Pocus.'
Fox has a live musical production of 'Grease' scheduled to air on January 31, 2016.
NBC recently announced plans to air a live version of 'The Wiz' later this year.
implications: The remake may attract a new audience and capitalize on the enduring popularity of the original film.
The special's production and airing schedule may impact Fox's programming strategy and viewer expectations.
The success of the remake could influence future adaptations of cult classics and musicals.
generated_content.conclusion: The development of 'The Rocky Horror Picture Show' remake marks a new chapter in Fox's efforts to adapt beloved musicals for the small screen.
